proposal: The Mandate recommends that NNSA make new warhead design and deployment a top priority, with new warheads for each leg of the triad, plutonium pit production in quantity at two sites (Los Alamos and Savannah River), and, if possible, reversal of the earlier decisions to retire the B83 bomb and cancel the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile. second_review.rule_applied: Implemented at the band floor. Test (a): the operative instruments of the ask are funding, continuation and maintenance, and these are in effect in substance: the two-site plan continues and, per a pre-enactment summary, is codified in the FY2026 NDAA; plutonium modernization, the W93 and W87-1 programs and the sea-launched cruise missile and its warhead are funded through P.L. 119-21 and FY2026 measures. Test (b): nothing is opposite to the ask; the B83 reversal is not shown and was qualified by the text as if possible. Test (c): funding requires Congress, and Congress has provided it. Quantity pit output is years away, but page 372 asks that such production be funded and pages 398 to 399 ask that two sites be maintained, not that a numeric milestone be met, so the missing output keeps the record at the floor rather than in in_progress.

status_summary: The two-site plutonium pit approach has continued: NNSA published a notice of intent for a programmatic environmental impact statement covering Los Alamos and Savannah River on 2025-05-09, and the draft became available on 2026-04-17, with comments open to 2026-07-16 and a final statement planned for early 2027. Section 3112 of Public Law 119-60 (FY2026 NDAA, enacted 2025-12-18) adds a capacity subsection, codified as 10 U.S.C. 6128(f), under which Los Alamos is to be able to produce at least 30 war reserve pits a year and Savannah River at least 50, with no separate deadline, while subsection (a) of that section keeps minimums of 30 pits during 2026 and 80 during 2030; and Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) provided 2 billion dollars for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile and 400 million dollars for its warhead, per CRS, which also notes statutory deployment dates of 2032 and 2034. Trade press reported on 2026-01-29 that Los Alamos exceeded its pit production objectives and is working toward 30 pits per year by 2028, and NNSA's release of 2026-10-16 states that the performance baseline (Critical Decision 2/3) for the Savannah River facility's main processing building was signed on 2026-10-15 with full start of construction authorized, and that Savannah River is to join Los Alamos as a pit production site once construction is complete. The stage is implemented because the funding, continued warhead development and two-site posture the text asks for are in effect, while quantity production is years away and no action on the B83 retirement was found.

timeline.event: NNSA published a notice of intent to prepare a programmatic environmental impact statement for plutonium pit production, with single-site and multi-site alternatives at Los Alamos and Savannah River.
Public Law 119-21 enacted; per CRS it includes 2 billion dollars for the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile and 400 million dollars to accelerate its warhead.

The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (S. 1071) is enacted as Public Law 119-60; Section 3112 adds a capacity subsection, now codified as 10 U.S.C. 6128(f) (the pit production section that section 3111 restated from the repealed 50 U.S.C. 2538a), requiring that Los Alamos have the capability to produce at least 30 war reserve pits a year and the Savannah River Plutonium Processing Facility at least 50, with no separate deadline for that capacity.
EPA published the notice of availability of the draft pit production programmatic environmental impact statement, opening a 90-day comment period to 2026-07-16, with public hearings in May 2026.

DOE signs Critical Decision 2/3, the approved performance baseline, for the Savannah River Plutonium Processing Facility main processing building and authorizes full start of construction; NNSA's release of 2026-10-16 says Savannah River will join Los Alamos as a second pit production site once construction is complete and gives no cost or schedule figures.

title: Fund new warheads, keep two plutonium pit sites, revive sea-launched cruise missile
uncertainties: Pit counts are classified, so progress rests on official statements relayed by trade press. The text of Section 3112 of Public Law 119-60 was read in an earlier review only in a reproduction of the GPO slip-law pages (139 Stat. 1462-1463) hosted by the Los Alamos Study Group, a non-government site. On 2026-10-22 the govinfo.gov HTML of the law was opened again: its table of contents lists section 3112 (plutonium pit production capacity) in Division C, Title XXXI, Subtitle B, but the readable text stops in Division A, so the operative wording still was not compared against a government-hosted body text; the uscode.house.gov page failed, and the law.cornell.edu page for 10 U.S.C. 6128, tried once in review, returned a Title 10 personnel table of contents instead of the section. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel's page for 10 U.S.C. 6128 (uscode.house.gov, current through Public Law 119-120, opened 2026-10-23; the code text, not the enrolled law) shows that the capacity provision now sits in subsection (f), with no fewer than 30 war reserve pits annually at Los Alamos and no fewer than 50 at Savannah River, and its source credit cites Public Law 119-60 sections 3111 and 3112 (139 Stat. 1363, 1461 and 1462); its notes say the section 3112 amendment was directed to section 4219 of the Atomic Energy Defense Act and executed to 10 U.S.C. 6128, and that similar provisions were in 50 U.S.C. 2538a until section 3111 repealed it, so the reference to 50 U.S.C. 2538a is the earlier codification. Subsection (a) of 10 U.S.C. 6128 keeps minimums of 30 pits during 2026 and 80 pits during 2030, so the statement that no deadline applies holds only for the capacity subsection, and (inference) the 2028 working target for 30 pits a year at Los Alamos sits behind a 2026 statutory minimum. The DOE hearing presentation (energy.gov) says a court settlement requires a record of decision on a set schedule; that litigation was not traced. A search for any decision to keep the B83 found nothing conclusive. An advocacy group's summary of the conference text, used as a lead only, also describes 210 million dollars for the cruise missile and 50 million dollars for its warhead and continued W93 and W87-1 funding; those amounts were not checked in the enacted text. The Los Alamos production report (Exchange Monitor, 2026-01-29) is a report of status, not a government action, and is kept as a source rather than a timeline event. Unverified leads from Arms Control Today (a publication of the Arms Control Association, September 2026, day not given), held at low confidence until an official document or news report confirms them: that construction of the Savannah River facility is at an early stage with completion expected between late 2031 and mid-2035; that officials said Los Alamos output could be accelerated by 2028; and that an internal review of pit plans was requested in the FY2026 appropriations act. NNSA's release of 2026-10-16 on the Savannah River baseline gives no cost or completion dates. Much of the two-site posture and warhead work predates 2025-01-20 and continues; the record reports alignment, not new causation. Overlaps the DoD-chapter record c04-06 on pits and the cruise missile.
